record._scope: Replaces the instance-ratio metric for every composition from this point on. Defined once here so the remaining compositions follow it.
record.supersedes: fourCompositions2026_08_31.instanceRatioMethodNote, and the 87.5% / 92% baselines the build prompt cited.
record.whyTheRatioWasDropped: The 87.5 and 92 figures came from a method that was never written down and could not be reproduced by any measure applied across six frames. A percentage that cannot be recomputed cannot be checked, and three different denominators (all authored nodes, excluding annotation, UI elements only) each gave a different answer with no principled way to choose. Do not re-baseline it and do not carry it forward.
record.theCheck: Binary, per frame: is any UI element drawn by hand where a published library component exists? Yes or no. Where yes, name the specific elements.
exemptions: SCAFFOLDING — an element drawn because a Figma instance cannot host children (a listbox that cannot be a Paper, a Menu past its four slots, a Table/Row that cannot take real cells).
ANNOTATION — headers, legends, captions, markers, section labels, anything that describes the frame rather than being an example in it.
INEXPRESSIBLE — a state, variant or content shape no published component can express (a selected ButtonGroup segment, a small-density table cell, a two-line Menu/Item).
record.reportingRule: Every hand-drawn UI element must be assigned to exactly one of the three exemption categories, or the answer is YES and it is a finding. Say which category each falls in.
record.whyThisIsBetter: It is what the ratio was a proxy for, it cannot drift, and a wrong answer is falsifiable by looking at the frame.
